rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to violating: chunk 2 "Prework": line 8: "This module meets the design question that follows: which checks belong at the seams, so the work does not queue on your read?" — it stays inside. (a) "He" (same line) resolves to Klaassen, named in the same sentence. (b) "the design question that follows" is not a forward pointer at a later slide: the question is unpacked after the colon on the same line, and "follows" reads as consequence-of-Klaassen's-practice, which the preceding sentence supplies in-chunk ("He measures a verifier before trusting it and runs several in parallel"). Post-a4920c15 the slide lost the sentence that had located the question against the M4 term and the M5 reading; what replaced it carries its own antecedent, so the sequential read no longer leans on either. (c) "the seams" is first-use in this file and mildly abstract, but it is a common-noun phrase unpacked by its own clause ("so the work does not queue on your read"), not a pronoun or demonstrative, and it is maintainer-attested at line 93 ("the M6 close stays concrete about checks at workflow seams"). Other chunks: chunk 5 "Human close" line 41 "the exercise's gap map and stack-map" and "the encode-move" resolve under the module-arc carve-out (the exercise is inlined at line 37, immediately before this chunk, in deck order) and via the `## What You'll Learn` signposting bullet "**Encode** the lesson" (line 18); chunk 6 line 56 "The three-pattern" is arc-earned spine vocabulary (grep: named in the-far-half.md, test-and-learn.md, what-packaging-is.md, diagnose-and-resend.md, learn-from-the-test.md); chunk 4 line 25 "The un-packaged Module 4 send-off. The packaged Module 5 re-send." names its referents outright.

Closest: chunk 8 "Next": line 76: "The training opened on a trick." — names the beat by its content (a trick), not by file position ("the opening lecture said…"), and the compendium's own §1 carve-out prints "the trick you named at the opening trick-exchange" as an accepted module-arc form; §2 also grants a closer summing the arc. The beat is real: grep for "trick" hits curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md and prework.md. Chunk 2's "Optional lookup pages" (line 10) are navigational pointers, NAMED not located ("session transcripts in the reference", "long-running shapes") — the §2 carve-out, and they carry no page-geometry locator.

Closest: chunk 1 "Big Idea" at 15 words (check-slide-size.js --report, smallest slide) — line 4: "Every gap you found belongs somewhere durable, or you will find it again next week." One self-carrying claim, no wait-state, no context-dependent single bullet. Chunk 5 "Human close" is the thinnest narrative slide and still states its own mode (line 41: "This slot is a human round: talk, compare, no prompts").

Closest: chunk 5 header "Human close" against its own content — line 41 "No compound prompt here… This slot is a human round: talk, compare, no prompts" and line 45's self-study variant. No contradiction: the header names the mode the chunk delivers. Maintainer accept-note at line 99 attests the beat is a pre-close, not the module ending, and the trailing sections are the design — honoured, not re-flagged. All other headers are the canonical module-shape section names and each chunk's content matches (Prework = pre-reads, Optional challenges = four optional items, Next = the carry-forward).

Per sub-item, over the body (lines 1-83): (a) "Not X. Not Y. Z." — `grep -nE '\bNot [A-Za-z]'` over the body returns rc=1, zero hits; (b) anaphora/epistrophe triples — chunk 4 line 25 runs a PAIR, not a triple ("One session gave you a failure mode to name. Two sessions give you gaps…"), and the second leg carries new content; (c) self-grading superlatives — none; closest is chunk 8 line 74 "The reading is the loop, not the sending", a claim about where the work is, no value-prop grading; (d) number + own retraction — no numbers in body; (e) abstraction-noun stacks — closest is chunk 6 line 61 "the durable shape is add, sharpen, delete", concrete verbs; (f) verb triplets with an empty leg — same line: add / sharpen / delete each answer "what does this concretely mean?" against a rules file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM: §9 exists to stop the bolded-lead-sentence monoculture that makes bold stop meaning "handle" — present in miniature here. chunk 8 "Next": line 78: "**Going deeper, when this loop has to scale past you:**" — a ten-word whole lead clause in bold, against the rule's "Bold the handle (≲5 words, a sub-span), never a whole lead sentence." The reading-list/lookup waiver (Antti 2026-08-13) turns off the per-slide COUNT, not the handle cap, and its instruction is to bold the mode word and leave the rest plain — the linked title here is already plain, so only the qualifier clause overruns. No maintainer accept-note covers this line (the file's notes cover the capstone sign-off, the rescue callouts, the Human close, and the KC independence axis — all honoured, none re-flagged). Non-blocking polish. Other bolds cleared, not charged: chunk 3's six LO verbs are the module-shape template (explicit §9 N/A, no accept-note owed); chunk 4's two rescue-callout leads sit under the standing accept-note at line 95; chunk 5's "**Self-study variant.**" is one two-word handle.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Shrink the bold to the mode word — "**Going deeper:**" — and let the condition run in plain text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.

Corroborated mechanically: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <target> --report` enumerates all 8 body slides including "Prework" (92 words), i.e. the module's own sections are inside the measured deck surface per §14's 2026-08-12 scope fix.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Unnumbered trailing clause: "`## Next` is two plain sentences: what the next module does, what the student carries into it (Antti 2026-08-14)."
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM the clause prevents: a closer that TEACHES steals the slide of the module it points at. Absent here — M6 is the terminal module of the AE101 core arc, so there is no next module's beat to front-run. The bans it also carries are all clean on chunk 8: no mechanism aside in parentheses, no housekeeping (nothing about closing the session or opening fresh), no term a later module coins. Lines 74-82 run past two sentences by design — the capstone sign-off ("Keep on learning and sharing." / "Antti") is maintainer-attested at line 91 as a deliberate check_writing §6 exception with "Future judges should not re-flag", and the arc-closing line 76 is a closer summing the deck (§2). No numbered rule behind this row; recorded so the clause is not silently skipped.
